Requirements:
- Start kimi web on loopback only: kimi web --no-open --allowed-host .ts.net
- Do not pass --host, do not pass --dangerous-bypass-auth, do not enable remote terminals or shutdown
- If kimi web is already running, restart it with the flags above
- Use Tailscale Funnel to publish kimi to the internet. Do not use Cloudflare Tunnel
- Install Tailscale and sign in if missing. If Funnel is not enabled yet, follow the CLI prompt to turn it on in the admin console or first-run dialog
- Read the local address from the kimi startup banner (strip #token=), then run: tailscale funnel --bg PORT. If bind and port were not changed, that is usually http://127.0.0.1:58627, so: tailscale funnel --bg 58627
- Do not expose Kimi on 0.0.0.0 or a LAN interface
- Funnel prints https://machine.ts.net when it is ready

Reply with one line:

A UPA plugin is discovered as MCP tools. Packages set ui.present when they ship surfaces and templates. The host paints that tree from _upa. If ui.present is false, or you turn off UI cards, the result stays text. This page is the frontend; Settings MCP remains a separate list of ordinary servers.

ui.present true means the package ships a surface tree. The host binds _upa into that tree in the chat bubble. Turn the toggle off to keep the current text result. Text-only packages set present false.

Listed as MCP tools so the model finds them. Invoke then returns data; UI packages also attach _upa.

Developers set memory.everme.trajectory in upa.json. true lets the host persist this call's arguments, vendor JSON, and template fill as an EverMe trajectory. Omit or false: redact plugin I/O and keep only the tool name. This does not write the durable Profile. Users can still turn EverMe memory off.
